messages:
incident-bot: PROD alert P0 — container crashloop detected in runtime-pool-prod. 1200 restarts in the last 10m across nodes g4dn-*-pool. Metric: pod_restart_rate > 300/m. Monitoring: https://grafana.company/alerts/alert/9234 :rotating_light:
Priya: acked, oncall here. starting triage. paging eng-runtime + sre-oncall.
Alice: on it, joining. I see a cluster of pods showing SIGSEGV in runtime_engine when loading TRT-fused kernels. grabbing a pod log now.
Ben: I'm with you. any customer 5xx spike?
Carla: CS dashboard shows a spike in error responses for 3 customers using large-ctx models. ~150 errors in last 5m, support page queued.
Alice: paste — pod log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T10:13:02Z] runtime_engine: initializing kernels
[2026-03-15T10:13:03Z] TRT fused loader: loaded 12 kernels
[2026-03-15T10:13:03Z] cuda: launchKernel failed: invalid device-pointer
[2026-03-15T10:13:03Z] runtime_engine(+0x1f4a3): Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

Priya: kubectl describe on one affected pod shows Back-off restarting failed container, restartCount=38. Events: Failed to start container; OOMKilled sometimes, other times Signal 11.
Ben: ok multiple failure modes. looks like either kernel illegal memory access or OOM depending on input length. Could be KV cache sizing + fused kernel bug.
Alice: I ran `gdb` on core — simplified trace:
```
#0  0x00007f3a2c8d1234 in fused_attention::compute() at fused_attention.cu:412
#1  0x00007f3a2c8c9abc in runtime_engine::run_chunk() at engine.cc:987
#2  0x000055b1a2d71234 in main_loop() at server.cc:122
```
Ben: we should isolate by disabling fused kernels on prod to stop segfaults. quick mitigation: set env REDWOOD_RUNTIME_ENABLE_FUSED=0 in runtime DaemonSet (or patch deployment). That will revert to reference kernels (slower but stable).
Priya: agreed. I'm going to patch node pool to cordon nodes flapping to avoid scheduling new pods there, and scale up replacement node group without the problematic NV driver (temporarily).
Alice: preparing deploy patch now. plan: 1) patch deployment to set REDWOOD_RUNTIME_ENABLE_FUSED=0; 2) rolling restart; 3) route traffic off older model variants for a few mins; 4) collect cores and upload to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/4390012000/ .
deploy-bot: trigger patch: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime --env=REDWOOD_RUNTIME_ENABLE_FUSED=0 --namespace=prod` — started.
deploy-bot: rollout status: deployment/runtime paused -> rollingupdate started (10 pods).
Ben: while rolling, put a soft global fallback rule: smart-router -> prefer model-compact v2 for new requests to reduce mem footprint. Eng-runtime, can you push that?
eng-runtime: done. Router policy updated to prefer model-compact-v2 for routes tagged non-enterprise. TTL 15m.
Carla: customer impact — which customers? names: BetaRetail, SearchCloud, DocWriterInc. Customer-facing severity: 2 for two customers, 1 for BetaRetail (experienced partial downtime). CS will send initial advisory and open escalation tickets.
Alice: logs show a small subset of pods hit CUDA "invalid device pointer" immediately before SIGSEGV. Suspect race in kernel load/unload path when certain sequence lengths > 16384. I've reproduced locally with a stress harness.
Priya: good repro. priority: stop production crashes. If fused disable reduces crashes to zero, we'll keep it until eng provides a patched build.
Ben: also enable auto-eviction policy on nodes showing >50% GPU memory thrash; set kubelet eviction.soft to reduce OOMKilled noise.
Alice: rolling patch finished. monitoring shows restart rate down 95% in 3m. No new SIGSEGV in patched pods so far.
incident-bot: Alert resolved (condition cleared).
Priya: nice. I'm going to collect the cores we have, strip symbols, and upload. leaving a task for eng-runtime to produce a reproducible patch.
Alice: taking ownership of root cause. I'm going to: 1) bisect fused-kernel commit range; 2) add guard checks for invalid device pointers; 3) add UT with long context lengths; target hotfix build: runtime-engine 1.14.2+hotfix.ETA 6h for build, 2h for internal canary.
Ben: I'll own the live mitigation checklist and postmortem. Adding follow-up actions: - add better health checks to detect kernel load failures - add rate-limiter at smart-router to prevent oversized ctx from triggering this on single node - improve core collection automation.
Carla: CS will draft sendable update. I'll coordinate with legal for customers on contracts impacted.
Priya: good. Oncall handoff: I'm handing to Ben in 2h for the PM window. Ben, you have the pager.
Ben: acknowledged, I'll monitor the canary and coordinate the postmortem. Please DM me any further customer escalations.
Alice: one more data point — a small percentage of incidents were OOMKilled at large batch sizes on nodes with mixed allocation. We'll also run a test to ensure KV cache capping avoids that.
Priya: recorded incident timeline, prepping a short blameless summary for ops.
Ben: tagging this for follow-up: ENG-RUNTIME-4390012000, SRE-4390012000. Postmortem owner: Ben.
Carla: closing loop with CS — sending initial customer note now.
incident-bot: Incident P0 -> P1 (mitigated) after config rollback / rollout (reason: disable fused kernels).
Priya: thanks team. we'll reconvene in 4h for RCA. :thumbsup:
